root_idea.summary: The root has two established semantic orientations: clearing material from a surface by sweeping, and withdrawing into concealment or a covert.
root_idea.development: The sweeping branch yields the broom, sweepings, and related agent nouns. The concealment branch yields the covert-dwelling animal and, by comparison, the stars or planets that disappear into their settings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural adjective كُنَّس is normalized to the singular active-participle citation form كَانِسٌ.

senses.definition: One who enters a covert or hiding-place, withdrawing from view.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural كُنَّس in 81:16 is interpreted as wild antelopes or wild cattle entering their coverts; another reported interpretation identifies the referents as angels. These are alternative referential interpretations of the concealment construction.

senses.definition: Of stars or planets: disappearing into their setting or becoming hidden beneath sunlight after traversing their courses.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression الجَوَارِي الكُنَّس, the celestial interpretation compares the bodies' disappearance to animals entering their coverts. Classical explanations include stars that run their course and set, the five visible planets, or stars hidden by the sun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sweep a house, chamber, or place with a broom, removing material from its surface.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the object may be a house, chamber, or other place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sweep people away or destroy them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of sweeping away; attested with the synonym كَسَحَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withdraw into a tent or a covered camel-litter and hide oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended use of entering a covert; the source attests both entering a tent and entering a camel-litter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covert, hiding-place, abode, or cave into which a gazelle or wild bovine retreats, especially for protection from heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for the animal's refuge; plural forms include أَكْنِسَةٌ, كُنُسٌ, and كُنَّسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sweepings or the dust removed by sweeping; also the place where such sweepings are thrown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word covers both the collected material and, in a related use, its disposal place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of worship associated with Christians or Jews; sometimes, a place of worship of unbelievers generally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation may refer to a church, synagogue, or—according to differing classical usage—to either category.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A branch-built, covered camel-litter or riding enclosure in which the occupant sits shaded and concealed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal sense derived from the notion of concealment.
Attested in the figurative expression مَكَانِسُ الرَّيْبِ; the figurative reading is marked as assumed in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A broom or other implement used for sweeping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary instrument noun; plural مَكَانِسُ.
An agent noun referring to the craft or occupation.
A rare lexical item recorded as a separate supplemental entry.

The supplied Lane discussion records multiple interpretations of 81:16, including celestial bodies, wild animals, and angels; the listed senses distinguish the concealment construction from its celestial application.
